old_description: We’re proud of our storied past, but our sights are set on the future. Every day, our goal is to better our process, planet, and customers’ business.
about:
Airlite Plastics Co. is a family-owned packaging manufacturer based in Omaha, Nebraska. The company does not disclose its founding year or original founders publicly, but describes itself as having a "storied past" with a future-first orientation.

The company produces a portfolio of in-mold labeled (IML) and round containers, lids, and drink cups, including containers with an EVOH oxygen barrier layer for extended shelf life and products designed to withstand high-pressure processing (HPP). Decoration capabilities include in-mold labeling, flexographic printing (up to eight colors with UV curing), and dry offset printing with in-house plate production. Airlite also offers custom graphics, package design, engineering, and marketing services. Specific facility size, headcount, and production volumes are not disclosed.

Airlite serves customers in temperature-controlled shipping, as well as markets for horticulture, household, and cultured products, with specific product lines for high-pressure processing (HPP) applications.

Airlite emphasizes its family-owned structure as a differentiator, citing responsiveness and long-term customer partnerships without bureaucratic delays. The company highlights a history of innovation in IML packaging, oxygen barrier technology, and HPP applications, and states it operates with a focus on sustainability and responsibility.

name: Akrivis Components and Tools
old_description: We supply hydro-cleaning systems, vapor degreasers, lead forming equipment, wire bonders, DI water systems, and other SMT manufacturing tools.
about:
Akrivis Components and Tools, based in Henderson, Nevada, was established in 2023 as a North American technical sales and support resource for specialized electronics manufacturing equipment. The company was created to bridge the gap between overseas equipment builders and North American manufacturers needing clearer communication, application review, installation, training, and service coordination.

The firm distributes a focused range of process equipment including hydro-cleaning systems, vapor degreasers, lead forming machines, component tinning systems, wire bonders, and thermal/vacuum heating equipment. Specific models offered include the Vapor SUI Mini compact vapor degreaser, the Hydro-clean LDS batch cleaning system, the Automatic Forming Machine APFL for lead forming, and the Semi-Automatic Bonder PW22 for microelectronics assembly. Beyond equipment supply, Akrivis provides application review, factory coordination, import and delivery logistics, installation and operator training, and post-sale service support from a Los Angeles-area support point covering the United States, Canada, and Mexico.

The company serves electronics manufacturers, labs, and production teams in reliability-critical sectors, primarily aerospace and defense electronics and medical device electronics. Customers typically engage Akrivis when they face specific process challenges such as residue removal, solderability restoration, component geometry control, cleaning workflows, bonding processes, or thermal/vacuum processing steps that require greater repeatability.

Akrivis differentiates itself by adopting an application-first support model that starts with the process requirement rather than a catalog page. The company emphasizes local, U.S.-based communication to overcome time-zone and language barriers, and it coordinates the full purchase scope — including freight, duties, installation, training, documentation, and warranty — before a purchase order is placed. This approach aims to reduce the risk of buying niche equipment directly from overseas builders.

name: Alabama Cable Telecomm Associates
old_description: Founded in 1965, ACBA serves as the advocate for our cable providers, operators, suppliers and programmers.
about:
Founded in 1965 in Montgomery, Alabama, the Alabama Cable & Broadband Association (ACBA) began as an advocacy organization for the state's cable providers, operators, suppliers, and programmers. The trade association operates as a non-profit entity representing the collective interests of Alabama's cable industry.

ACBA does not manufacture physical products; instead, it provides legislative advocacy, regulatory representation, and policy analysis on behalf of its members. The association engages in the legislative process on policy, regulatory, and taxation issues affecting the cable and telecommunications sector. Its work supports an industry that employs more than 3,000 people across Alabama, delivers over 26,000 direct and indirect jobs, and generates a $3.56 billion economic impact. The association also coordinates industry contributions of millions of dollars in cash, in-kind support, and volunteer time to local charities.

The association's membership comprises cable providers, network operators, equipment suppliers, and programming companies operating in Alabama. Its advocacy spans broadband deployment, telecommunications regulation, and spectrum policy, with recent focus on the state's broadband expansion initiatives and shared spectrum debates. ACBA positions the cable industry as a key partner in Alabama's education system, economic development, and quality of life.

ACBA's founding purpose remains its core differentiator: providing a unified voice for the cable industry throughout the legislative process. The organization works to ensure the industry remains competitive amid rapid technological change in information and communication services across the state. This advocacy model distinguishes ACBA as the primary representative body for Alabama's cable and broadband sector.

name: Alan Wire Company
old_description: Alan Wire has proudly served and supplied the electrical community as a dependable manufacturer of high-quality wire and cable products for 50 years. Based in Sikeston, Missouri, AW offers copper and aluminum 600-volt wire and cable products for commercial, industrial, and utility markets.
about:
Alan Wire Company operates from Sikeston, Missouri, where founder Alan Keenan started the business in a family garage. The company remains family-owned, now led by Keenan alongside his sons Scott and Jonathan, who serve in executive roles.

The company manufactures copper and aluminum 600-volt wire and cable products for commercial, industrial, and utility markets. Its product lines include copper building wire (THHN, NM-B, XHHW-2, TFFN), aluminum building wire (THHN, XHHW-2, SER, URD), bare copper grounding products, and service entrance cable. Production runs 24 hours a day, five days a week in a one-million-square-foot facility staffed by approximately 500 employees.

Alan Wire serves electrical distributors, contractors, and end users across commercial construction, residential building, industrial power and control, and utility sectors. Its network of qualified sales representatives supports customers nationwide, with the Sikeston location positioned within a day's drive of over 60% of the U.S. population.

The company's stated differentiator is an "easy to do business with" philosophy emphasizing direct answers, minimal bureaucracy, consistent quality, and taking responsibility for mistakes. This culture traces back to Keenan's founding principles of hard work, fair treatment, and common courtesy.

name: Alanic - Wholesale Clothing Manufacturers
old_description: We are the biggest clothing wholesaler and manufacturer since 2004
about:
Alanic, a wholesale clothing manufacturer, was founded in 2004 and is headquartered in North Hollywood, California. The company operates globally with sales and operations offices in Los Angeles, Connecticut, Dubai, Sydney, and London.

The company designs and manufactures men’s, women’s, and children’s apparel spanning fashion, fitness, activewear, sportswear, and accessories such as bags, caps, and socks. Alanic offers white-label and private-label manufacturing, custom design services, and low minimum order quantities for startups. Its production facility includes cutting, hot stamping, sewing, weaving, and technology R&D workshops, and it runs a sustainable clothing program that transforms recycled fishing nets, plastic bottles, and worn garments into nylon 7 chips and organic fibers for biodegradable products.

Alanic serves retailers, business owners, bulk buyers, and private-label brands across the fashion, fitness, activewear, sportswear, and children’s clothing sectors. Customers include startups launching new lines and established brands seeking eco-friendly collections.

The company differentiates itself with a low MOQ policy, full customization support including pre-production samples, a sustainable production process that recycles waste into new fibers, 24/7 customer support, and worldwide low-cost shipping.

name: Albuquerque Apparel Center
old_description: Albuquerque Apparel Center is an infrastructure tailored to meet the needs of designers, suppliers, production houses, merchants, and visitors with a wide range of useful customized products and services.  We are New Mexico’s premier venue of clothing and accessory design as well as supplies, services and events.
about:
Albuquerque Apparel Center operates in Albuquerque, New Mexico, as a physical and online hub for the state's apparel and accessory industry. The center was established to connect designers, suppliers, production houses, merchants, and visitors with resources, supplies, employment, and industry-related services.

The center provides a range of services including a networking hub with multi-media promotional advertising and events such as fashion shows and seminars, a retail outlet where designers can sell directly to customers while connecting with wholesale buyers, and an online destination site, NMFashionInfo.com, listing apparel stores, supplies, services, and events across New Mexico. It also runs the AAC School of Fashion Design, offering classes in flat pattern design, draping, sewing, and couture garment construction for all ages, along with mentorship programs for schools and organizations. Custom design and pattern services are available for start-ups and established businesses.

The center serves the broader fashion and apparel industry in New Mexico, targeting independent designers, apparel start-ups, production houses, retail merchants, and educational institutions. It also works with community organizations such as battered women's groups and rehabilitation facilities, providing fashion design classes as a pathway to employment and self-sufficiency.

The center's stated mission is to foster the growth of New Mexico's apparel industry by leveraging the state's unique Southwest, Native American, and Western styles, lower cost of living, and local creative talent. It positions itself as a support system that guides businesses from concept to consumer, aiming to create jobs and retain the economic benefits of New Mexico's distinctive fashion heritage within the state.
